source.title: On the Role of Bidirectionality in Language Model Pre-Training
source.authors: Mikel Artetxe; Jing-Fei Du; Naman Goyal; Luke Zettlemoyer; Ves Stoyanov

record.file_problem: not stated; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports held-out perplexity across model sizes and downstream accuracy across sizes, but does not fit or test scaling-law equations. It is a conceptual test of scale-related outcomes, not a reproduction of the original law-fitting method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports perplexity by model size in Tables 3–4 and average fine-tuning accuracy by size in Table 9. It does not fit power laws, report exponents, extrapolate from small runs, or sweep training tokens or compute to find an optimal allocation. Table 4 also varies inference-time bidirectional attention; only its endpoint settings are retained here. Other per-task downstream scores and zero-shot results are not included as rows because the reported aggregate fine-tuning results already test V6 and the row limit would otherwise be exceeded.
record.test_reason: The study tests V6 through downstream accuracy across 125M–6.7B models with controlled pretraining variants. It reports loss-related size trends relevant to V1, but does not establish a power-law form. Its principal contribution is a new setting involving bidirectionality and pretraining objectives.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that the optimal bidirectionality configuration depends on application and that most differences persist over the tested scale range. They also identify an exception: scale reduces the infilling penalty of combining masking with next-token prediction when a bidirectional prefix is used. They do not establish fitted scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares language-model pretraining objectives and bidirectionality settings across model sizes; it does not fit or test the original scaling-law equations.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with pretraining objective, evaluation setting, and use of bidirectional attention; the authors say the effects depend on application.

fits_no_version.finding: Bidirectionality and objective choices change application-specific performance, with some gaps persisting as models grow.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The best pretraining objective and attention configuration depend on the application, even across increasing model sizes. This alone does not demonstrate V4 architecture-shape invariance or V7 fit-dependence.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The paper reports discrete size points without uncertainty estimates or scaling-law fits. Training-token and compute scaling are not varied. Several variants are trained at only two sizes, and the authors note that bidirectional-prefix or masking variants receive fewer tokens of supervision.
record.rows_left_out: Table 4's intermediate rbidir values and Tables 5–8 and 10's separate infilling, zero-shot, and per-task fine-tuning results are not included; the reported aggregate Table 9 fine-tuning scores were retained for V6. No rows are omitted from Tables 3 or 9.

untested.parts: Power-law form, exponents, several orders of magnitude, and non-bottleneck conditions are not established. All models receive 100B training tokens; perplexity must be log-transformed to obtain cross-entropy loss.
No prediction of large-run loss from small-run fits.
No controlled depth/width or comparable architecture-shape sweep at fixed parameters; objective and attention changes are confounded with supervision.
No power-law test in another modality or training regime; fine-tuning accuracy alone does not establish this version.
No quantitative predictive fit, held-out scale extrapolation, or calibrated relationship between downstream performance and pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitted exponents, compute-optimal splits, fitting choices, or demonstrated departures from a fitted power law.

missing.what: Unrecorded Table 9 attention arms: NXTUNI rbidir=1; NXTPRE rbidir=0; MSKUNI rbidir=1; MSKBI rbidir=0; HYBUNI rbidir=1; HYBPRE rbidir=0. These include plateaus and declines relevant to conditional downstream scaling. rows_left_out does not declare their omission.

record.verdict_notes: No V1 verdict is warranted from decreasing perplexities alone. V6 support concerns observed directional trends, with quantitative prediction untested. Fine-tuning scores are best development results across a hyperparameter grid, without uncertainty estimates. Tables 5–8 and 10 are explicitly declared omitted, so their results are not listed as missing. The gate note incorrectly says Table 4 endpoints were retained; no Table 4 rows appear.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports perplexity at several parameter counts, but does not fit power laws or exponents, sweep tokens or compute, or establish that other variables are not bottlenecks.
No small-run fit is used to predict larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token trend is tested.
The study varies pretraining objectives and attention/context bidirectionality, not depth or width at fixed parameter count.
The study is limited to text pretraining; other modalities, repeated data, and transfer regimes are not tested.
The paper reports aggregate fine-tuning accuracy across model sizes, but does not fit a predictive relationship or relate downstream scores to pretraining loss.
The paper does not compare law-fitting methods, parameter-counting choices, schedules, or data setups for their effects on exponents or compute-optimal allocations.

relationships.condition: Reported fine-tuning attention configurations, from 125M through 2.7B; NXTPRE and MSKUNI through 355M
relationships.reason: The linked size series all improve in aggregate fine-tuning accuracy; for example T9-NXTUNI-125 to T9-NXTUNI-2.7B rises from 83.6 to 88.7.
relationships.display_finding: Every specified size series improved aggregate accuracy, including NXTUNI from 83.6 to 88.7.

relationships.condition: MSKBI and HYBPRE with bidirectional fine-tuning, and HYBUNI with unidirectional fine-tuning, 2.7B–6.7B
relationships.reason: T9-MSKBI, T9-HYBPRE and T9-HYBUNI at these sizes improve by 0.2, 0.5 and 0.2 points respectively.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy improved by 0.2 points for MSKBI, 0.5 for HYBPRE and 0.2 for HYBUNI.

relationships.reason: T9-NXTUNI-2.7B and T9-NXTUNI-6.7B show a plateau, 88.7 versus 88.6, despite continued perplexity improvement; uncertainty is unavailable.
relationships.display_finding: T9-NXTUNI scores stayed at 88.7 and 88.6 for 2.7B and 6.7B despite improving perplexity.

relationships.condition: Alternative fine-tuning attention settings at larger sizes
relationships.reason: From Table 9 text, omitted rows show HYBPRE rbidir=0 plateauing at 88.2, HYBUNI rbidir=1 declining 85.0→84.7, and MSKBI rbidir=0 declining 81.9→81.6 before recovering; scaling gains depend on attention configuration.
relationships.display_finding: HYBPRE with rbidir=0 plateaued at 88.2, HYBUNI with rbidir=1 declined from 85.0 to 84.7, and MSKBI with rbidir=0 fell from 81.9 to 81.6 before recovering.
